_comment: PORT campaign: the TYPES of IBM Spyre deeptools' `dsc/` data model, into
crates/compiler/deeptools. Its units are CLASS DEFINITIONS AND THEIR FIELDS, not algorithms.
The scope is four headers, VENDORED BYTE-IDENTICAL from the authority tree (verified with `cmp`
at staging time) rather than extracted: unlike a function-body campaign there is nothing to cut,
so there is no extraction to get wrong and no banner convention to follow. The whole declaration
of every type is present, in its original order, with its original comments.
READ crustify-types/AGENT-BRIEF.md IN FULL BEFORE EDITING ANYTHING.

_comment_deferred_not_dropped: ⛔ SCOPE BY WHAT THE ARCHITECTURE WILL NEVER NEED, NOT BY WHAT WE DO NOT SUPPORT TODAY.
A field this campaign does not carry gets a DEFERRED unit citing its C++ line, never a silent

_comment_acceptance: ⛔⛔ THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS THAT THE TRAIT CARRIER LAYER GOES AWAY, NOT THAT ITS STUBS GET BODIES.
schedule/stages/ddc_state.rs's header states the defect against itself: `currDsc` in the reference
IS sdsc.dscs_.at(idx); here it is a CLONE taken at construction, select_and_parse_ddl_template
writes through sdsc.dscs_mut().at_mut(idx) (ddc/v1.rs:6489), `those writes do NOT reach this
clone`, and `no caller can close it`. The cause is the ported signature: run_v1(sdsc: &mut
SuperDsc, sites: &mut P, ..) (ddc/v1.rs:6532) takes TWO independent &mut where the reference has
ONE object, so the borrow checker forces the clone and the write is dropped — and it compiles.
So schedule/stages/{ddc_store,ddc_store2,ddc_state,ddc_sites,ddc_tree,ddc_reads,offsets,env}.rs
are to be DELETED, not completed, once the types carry their own fields. 54 further stubs are
already unreachable behind four getters in reads.rs that return None; deleting the layer retires
those too. ⭐ A UNIT WHOSE ONLY EFFECT IS TO GIVE A TRAIT METHOD A BODY IS A PORT OF THE WRONG
THING — say so in the report instead of doing it.
⛔⛔ THAT DELETION IS NOT A UNIT OF THIS CAMPAIGN AND NOT A LICENCE TO DELETE CARRIER CODE. It
needs every type landed first and Ddc::run_v1 is in ddc/ddcv1.cpp, outside this target. Changing
a type's shape WILL break the carriers reading its old fields (wave 1: `error[E0560]: struct
ConditionNode has no field named then_region` in stages/ddc_tree.rs and stages/ddc_store2.rs).
The only acceptable repair is to ADAPT THE CALL SITE, carrying every effect across — never delete
the logic, never make a live call todo!(), never drop a branch because the new shape made it
awkward. A shrinking line count under stages/ is not progress here. See AGENT-BRIEF.md §3 for the
standard to match: acdf5a01b turned a `return None` refusal into an UNREPRESENTABLE state via
CondRegions and rewrote every caller with its loop intact.
⛔ THE GATE IS NOT AN ANCHOR COUNT. An anchor count is what let `1,076 units ported` mean 238
stubs. A unit is DONE only with all three: (1) zero todo! in its body for the arms this campaign
scopes, (2) a REAL NON-TEST CALLER named in the report, and (3) A FIELD COUNT — how many of the
C++ type's declared fields the Rust type now carries, and which it still does not, each with its
path:line. Point (3) is this campaign's burndown, and it is the number whose absence let 101
stubs accumulate: DesignSpaceConfig measured 9 of 49 on the Rust type (19 more elsewhere in the
crate, 21 nowhere) on 2026-09-16.
⛔ REPORT PER UNIT, NEVER PER CAMPAIGN. A campaign cannot audit its own boundary.
The build gate is `cargo check -p deeptools` + `cargo test -p deeptools`; never the workspace and
never the acceptance build from an agent worktree (~6 GB of target/ each).
